issues.t: Dual-clutch transmission shudder and jerky low-speed driving
issues.sym: Shudder or a jolt when pulling away, slow or hard engagement into Drive or Reverse, a bump between 2nd and 3rd gear, or jerky behavior in stop-and-go traffic. In bad cases it can slip or refuse to drive.
issues.why: The CLA uses an automated dual-clutch gearbox. Its wet clutch packs wear, its fluid degrades and its mechatronic control unit can fail, especially with lots of city driving and skipped fluid services. AMG versions wear their clutches faster.
issues.next: Ask a dealer whether the latest transmission software is installed. A fluid and filter change with a clutch adaptation reset often cures early shudder. Persistent slipping needs a transmission specialist.

issues.t: Water pump failure and overheating
issues.sym: The temperature gauge climbs, a coolant warning comes on, coolant goes missing, or the heater blows cooler air. Failure can be sudden.
issues.why: The water pump's plastic impeller can come loose from its shaft or the pump fails, so coolant stops circulating. The electronic thermostat wears out too. Owners report failures as early as about 23,000 miles.
issues.next: Pull over and shut the engine off if it overheats; driving on can blow the head gasket. Replace the pump and thermostat together.

issues.t: Timing chain rattle on cold start
issues.sym: A rattle from the front of the engine for a few seconds after a cold start, sometimes with a check engine light and camshaft sensor codes.
issues.why: The hydraulic chain tensioner can lose pressure overnight, letting the chain slap until oil pressure builds. Long oil change intervals and low oil speed up chain stretch.
issues.next: Have it checked soon, before the chain stretches far enough to jump teeth. Keep the oil at the right level with the correct Mercedes-approved oil.

issues.t: Turbocharger wear or failure
issues.sym: Blue or gray smoke under acceleration, a whine or grinding from the turbo, and loss of power.
issues.why: Turbo bearings wear when oil changes are stretched, the wrong oil is used, or the car is driven hard straight after a cold start.
issues.next: Have boost and oil leaks checked. Fix it early, because a failing turbo can send debris or oil into the engine and exhaust.

issues.t: Carbon buildup on intake valves
issues.sym: Rough idle, hesitation, misfires and less power, especially at low engine speeds.
issues.why: With direct fuel injection, fuel never washes the intake valves, so oil vapor from the crankcase vent bakes onto them as carbon.
issues.next: If a misfire code points to carbon, have the intake valves cleaned (walnut blasting). Regular highway driving and on-time oil changes help.

issues.t: Camshaft welds can fail (recall)
issues.sym: Sudden loss of power, ticking or knocking from the top of the engine, a stall, or an engine that won't restart.
issues.why: Camshafts on some engines built from July 17 to August 31, 2015 were welded out of specification and could break. Mercedes recalled them for free camshaft replacement.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall at a dealer or nhtsa.gov.

issues.t: Driver airbag could deploy unexpectedly (recall)
issues.sym: Often an airbag warning light from a broken clockspring. In rare cases the driver airbag could go off without a crash.
issues.why: Parts of the steering column were not grounded well enough. If the clockspring is broken, static electricity could trigger the driver airbag. Mercedes added grounding under recall.
issues.next: Check that the recall is done. If the airbag light is on, get it diagnosed; the recall adds grounding but does not replace a broken clockspring.

issues.t: Starter current limiter can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no sign in normal use. The risk comes when the starter is cranked over and over while the engine can't turn.
issues.why: Repeated cranking against an engine or transmission that won't turn can overheat the starter current limiter, which could cause a fire. Mercedes recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. If the engine won't turn over, don't keep cranking it; call for help.

issues.t: Front roof panel can come loose after a repair (recall)
issues.sym: Wind noise or a lifting edge at the front of the panoramic roof. In the worst case the panel could detach while driving.
issues.why: On cars with the panoramic roof, the panel between the windshield and the sunroof may not have been bonded correctly during an earlier repair. Mercedes recalled affected cars to replace the panel.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall, especially if the roof or windshield was ever repaired.

issues.t: Rearview camera image doesn't show (recall)
issues.sym: The screen stays black or shows no camera picture when reversing, or the infotainment screen goes black and reboots.
issues.why: Software errors in the camera system and, on 2020 to 2021 cars, the MBUX infotainment system could stop the camera image from appearing. Mercedes fixed both with free software updates.
issues.next: Make sure both software updates were installed, by a dealer or over the air. Use your mirrors carefully until then.

issues.t: Emergency call (eCall) may not work (recall)
issues.sym: An SOS system warning may appear, or there may be no sign. After a crash the car might not call for help or might send the wrong location.
issues.why: Software errors in the communication module and its SIM card could disable the emergency call system or send an incorrect location.
issues.next: Make sure the free software updates were done, over the air or at a dealer.

issues.t: Coolant line leak and coolant warning
issues.sym: A coolant level warning on the dash, coolant smell, or a puddle of coolant under the front of the car.
issues.why: A coolant line can leak because of high pressure inside the cooling system. Mercedes issued a service campaign for 2020 to 2021 CLA and GLA models.
issues.next: Check the coolant level when the engine is cold and ask a dealer whether the service campaign applies to your VIN. Don't drive if it is overheating.

issues.t: Car won't unlock or start with 'Battery - Start Engine' message
issues.sym: The car won't unlock or start, shows a 'Battery - Start Engine' message, or the battery is flat after sitting.
issues.why: A Mercedes bulletin traces this to a module keeping the car's data network awake after it is parked, which drains the battery.
issues.next: Jump-start or charge the battery, then have a dealer check for software updates and test the battery properly.

issues.t: Creaking or grinding from steering column
issues.sym: Creaking, squeaking, chattering or grinding when you turn the wheel, sometimes from between the steering wheel and the stalks.
issues.why: Mercedes has several bulletins on steering column noises on these cars, including a squeaking input shaft from too little grease.
issues.next: Have a dealer check it against the service bulletins; the fix is often lubrication or a part replacement under warranty.

issues.t: Front brakes squeal when stopping
issues.sym: A squeal from the front brakes as the car comes to a stop.
issues.why: Mercedes issued a bulletin for front brake squeal on these cars. It says braking performance is not affected.
issues.next: Mention the bulletin to the dealer. Have the pads checked if the noise turns into grinding.

issues.t: Chirping or tapping from engine pulley when cold
issues.sym: A chirp or tap from the front of the engine at cold start that fades as the engine warms up.
issues.why: Mercedes issued a bulletin on noise from the crankshaft pulley area on cold engines.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to check it against the bulletin while the car is under warranty.

issues.t: Humming or vibration from rear axle when maneuvering
issues.sym: A hum, vibration or noise from the rear when parking, turning tightly or pulling away. Seen on 4MATIC all-wheel-drive cars.
issues.why: Mercedes issued a bulletin for rear axle noise when maneuvering or moving off.
issues.next: Have a dealer check it against the bulletin. A drivetrain fluid or software fix may be needed.

issues.t: Driver door lock switch can corrode, risking rollaway (recall)
issues.sym: The car doesn't warn that the driver's door is open, and the parking brake or Auto-Park doesn't set itself when you open the door.
issues.why: A small switch inside the driver's door lock can corrode and fail to sense an open door, so the automatic parking brake may not engage. Mercedes is replacing the lock for free.
issues.next: Always put the car in Park and set the parking brake yourself until the recall is done. Check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Rear brake caliper bolts may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: Rattling or knocking from a rear wheel, or weaker braking.
issues.why: Fasteners on the rear brake caliper housing may not have been tightened properly, so brake parts could loosen or come off.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and have the free inspection done.

issues.t: Missing rear brake pad wear gauge (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom while driving. The car may lack the gauge used to check rear brake pad wear.
issues.why: Some cars shipped without the rear pad inspection gauge and owner's manual instructions required by federal rules.
issues.next: Have the dealer install the gauge, and have the rear pads checked at each service.
